items.title: Trump says AI safety fears a 'hoax' as he rejects calls for greater safeguards
items.description: The US president's comments come after Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told the BBC an AI "kill switch" may need to be mandatory.

items.title: AI regulation faces political deadlock as calls grow for Congress to act
items.description: With Trump opposed and Congress divided, new safety legislation on AI is unlikely to pass anytime soon despite mounting pressure.

items.title: Denmark says Russian warship fired flares at military helicopter
items.description: The Danish prime minister has accused Russia of "reckless" behaviour, while the Kremlin is yet to comment.

items.title: Welsh actor Matthew Rhys makes Emmy Awards history with double win
items.description: He becomes the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night at the prestigious TV ceremony.

items.title: Suspected sabotage causes major Netherlands rail disruption
items.description: Trains were cancelled or delayed on Tuesday after objects were found on tracks at multiple locations.

items.title: US confirms for first time it has deployed space weapons
items.description: The US Air Force Secretary says the weapons are necessary to defend the country against enemy action.

items.title: Donald Trump Jr and Bettina Trump say Putin ally paid for some wedding festivities as a 'gift'
items.description: An Instagram post from the couple said two nights of their wedding festivities in the Bahamas were partially funded by Umar Kremlev.

items.title: Nato jets down drone that entered Lithuanian airspace
items.description: The origin of the drone is currently unknown, but authorities say it likely entered Lithuania from neighbouring Belarus, an ally of Russia.

items.title: Legendary costume designer Bob Mackie dies aged 87
items.description: The "Sultan of Sequins" created iconic and dazzling costumes for stars including Cher, Tina Turner and Elton John.

items.title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate
items.description: Scientists say the record-breaking journey by three brothers offers hope wildlife can survive growing pressures.

items.title: China criticises idea it is in 'malicious competition' over AI
items.description: It follows the Anthropic CEO's calls for a slowdown in AI development - but in a way that prevents China from pulling ahead in the race.

items.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump's plan to restrict mail-in ballots
items.description: The Trump administration had asked the court to lift a federal judge's temporary block on new rules for mail-in ballots.

items.title: China tightens travel restrictions for citizens
items.description: Observers say the new rules will further tighten the Chinese government's control over its citizens.

items.title: Israeli minister threatens to revoke filmmakers' citizenship over Gaza documentary
items.description: The film accuses the Israeli army of mass civilian killing in Gaza, and Israeli officials say it could be treasonous.

items.title: US scraps limits on emissions from coal and gas power plants
items.description: The Environment Protection Agency says the move will save the country billions of dollars and reduce energy prices.

items.title: Malaysian boy acquitted for murder of schoolgirl on grounds of insanity
items.description: The killing of the 16-year-old nearly a year ago had shocked Malaysia and sparked debate about social media.

items.title: Immigrants held in small outdoor cages at 'Alligator Alcatraz' in Florida, investigators find
items.description: DHS inspectors say they found the immigration-detention centre violated basic standards for hygiene, medical care, food and safety.

items.title: Africa's richest man launches continent's biggest share sale
items.description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote says he wants ordinary people to share in the success of his oil refinery.

items.title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire
items.description: The state post service delivers pensions, medicine and letters to people just miles from the front.

items.title: Russians seek answers over hundreds missing after Ukraine's 2024 incursion
items.description: Officials say more than 300 Russians remain missing after the 2024 Kursk offensive, but no-one really knows the true figure.
